question: ‘Freedom is my birth right and I shall have it’. Who among the following said this?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bal Gangadhar Tilak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an Indian nationalist, teacher, and independence activist.
 
• He was one of the first leaders of the Indian Independence Movement and is considered "The Father of Indian Unrest".
 
• Tilak was a strong advocate of Swaraj (self-rule) and his famous declaration, "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it!" became a rallying cry for Indian nationalists.
 
• He was part of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio, which included Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal, who were prominent leaders in the early phase of the Indian independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai**

 
 
• Also known as Punjab Kesari, Lala Lajpat Rai was a prominent Indian freedom fighter and played a pivotal role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was associated with the Arya Samaj and was part of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio.
 
• He is remembered for his role in the protest against the Simon Commission, during which he sustained injuries leading to his death.
 
 
 
• **Aurobindo Ghosh**
 
 
• Sri Aurobindo was an Indian philosopher, yogi, and nationalist.
 
• He was one of the early leaders of the Indian independence movement and later turned to spiritual pursuits.
 
• He founded the Sri Aurobindo Ashram in Pondicherry.
 
 
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal**
 
 
• He was a prominent Indian nationalist, orator, and a member of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio.
 
• Pal was a strong advocate of Swadeshi and the boycott of British goods as a form of protest against colonial rule.
 
• He is regarded as the 'Father of Revolutionary Thoughts' in India.
